clue.text: Mysterious holy man buzzed with energy

indicators.note: with means the energy letter is added alongside the earlier pieces

parts.note: ST is the abbreviation for saint
a doorbell that buzzed rang
E is the physics symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A strange holy man is buzzing with nervous energy, like a mystic in a trance.
explanation.definitionFit: Something strange is odd and hard to explain, which is what mysterious describes.

clue.text: Quietly feeding dogs upset by simple tail trim

indicators.note: by means placed next to, so the last piece is set beside the rest
in a down clue, upset suggests turning something upside down, so the word is read bottom to top
feeding puts something into a mouth, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: curs are mongrel dogs
P is piano, the musical direction for quietly

indicators.note: the tail of a word is its final letter only

parts.note: the final letter of simple

explanation.surface: A dog groomer gives the hounds a quick trim at the tail, and they are upset about it.
explanation.walkthrough: Trim is the adjective here, meaning neat, not the verb that the dog-grooming picture suggests.
explanation.definitionFit: Spruce as an adjective means neat and smart in appearance, a synonym of trim as in a trim figure.

clue.text: Let slip clergyman brewed ale

indicators.note: brewing mixes and transforms ingredients, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: Rev is short for Reverend, a clergyman's title
the three letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A vicar, loosened up by home-brewed beer, blurts out a secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To let slip a secret is to disclose it accidentally, so both mean making something known.

clue.text: After English and French denials, perhaps hearing is straightforward

indicators.note: after places the final piece behind the earlier pair of refusals

parts.note: the English word of denial
the French word for no
hearing is one example of a sense, as perhaps signals

explanation.surface: Someone who has refused in two languages is now said to be speaking plainly.
explanation.walkthrough: English denials and French denials share the word denials: one refusal in each language.
explanation.definitionFit: A no-nonsense approach is direct and practical, the same idea as straightforward behaviour without fuss.

clue.text: Rowing crew's heaviness cut lead

indicators.note: cutting the lead removes whatever comes first, so the opening letter goes

parts.note: weight is how heavy something is

explanation.surface: A rowing crew complains that its weight is slowing it down, so it has lost the lead.
explanation.definitionFit: A racing boat with eight oarsmen is called an eight, and the name also covers its crew.

clue.text: Exercise in pushy manipulation builds excitement

indicators.note: manipulation handles and reshapes something, so these letters are rearranged
in means one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: the five letters rearranged
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A lesson in aggressive manipulation, the sort of course a hard-sell marketer might attend.
explanation.definitionFit: To hype up an event is to promote it energetically, generating anticipation and enthusiasm among the public.

clue.text: Funny clip of Mr Benn is capturing your heart

indicators.note: capturing holds something inside, so one piece goes within the other
clipping trims off the end, so the name loses its last letter

parts.note: Hilary Benn is a British Labour politician
taken as written

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its central part

parts.note: the two middle letters of your

explanation.surface: A clip from Mr Benn, the children's cartoon, is so charming it wins your heart.
explanation.walkthrough: Mr Benn suggests the old children's TV cartoon, but it is the politician Hilary Benn, with his first name clipped.
explanation.definitionFit: Hilarious means extremely amusing, a stronger form of funny.

clue.text: Settled with priest's help

parts.note: P is the abbreviation for priest
aid is assistance

explanation.surface: A debt was cleared with the help of the local priest.
explanation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: once a bill or account is cleared by handing over the money owed, the debt is closed.

clue.text: Successful record beaten after defeat

indicators.note: after places the word for beaten behind the word for defeat

parts.note: to smash an opponent is to defeat them heavily
hit means struck or beaten

explanation.surface: A sports record has been broken after a heavy loss.
explanation.walkthrough: Record looks like a sporting best, but it is a piece of recorded music.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash hit is a hugely popular song or show, so a successful record fits.

clue.text: Designs Prada top and bottom with model birds

indicators.note: with means the remaining pieces are added alongside
in a down clue the top and bottom of a word are its first and final letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of Prada
the Model T was the classic Ford car
terns are seabirds

explanation.surface: A fashion house's tops and skirts are shown off by models on a catwalk.
explanation.walkthrough: Prada, top, bottom and model all point to a fashion show; birds is British slang for young women, adding to the false picture.
explanation.definitionFit: Patterns are decorative designs, such as those printed on fabric or wallpaper.

clue.text: Bird's plucky, heading off north

indicators.note: heading off removes the head, the first letter of the word

parts.note: plucky means courageous
N is the compass abbreviation

explanation.surface: A brave bird sets off, heading north.
explanation.walkthrough: Heading off looks like setting out on a journey, but it means removing the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The raven is a large black crow, a species of bird.

clue.text: Dashing young man grabs four to go off and have fun

indicators.note: grabbing takes hold of something, so one piece is held inside the other

parts.note: a gallant is a fashionable, dashing young man
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A dashing young man takes a foursome off for a good time.
explanation.definitionFit: To gallivant is to roam about in search of pleasure and entertainment, often irresponsibly.

clue.text: Secures rent from business with many outlets

parts.note: chains fastens or secures something
rent as a past tense of rend, meaning ripped

explanation.surface: A landlord secures rent payments from a big retail business.
explanation.walkthrough: Rent looks like money paid to a landlord, but it is the past tense of rend, to tear.
explanation.definitionFit: A chain store is one of many shops under the same ownership, so the business has many branches.

clue.text: Woman's harbouring love for footwear

indicators.note: harbouring shelters something within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: she refers to a woman
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A woman nurses a passion for shoes.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoe is an item worn on the foot, a single example of footwear.

clue.text: Turned sunward outside chapter house for early morning song

indicators.note: turned means changed around, so these letters are rearranged
outside means the rearranged letters wrap around the other pieces

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged
C is an abbreviation for chapter
HO is the abbreviation for house

explanation.surface: Turned towards the rising sun outside the chapter house, monks sing their morning office.
explanation.definitionFit: The dawn chorus is the burst of birdsong at daybreak, a song of the early morning.

clue.text: Explain root potential of research

indicators.note: potential is what something could become, so these letters can be made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the eleven letters rearranged

explanation.surface: A request to explain the underlying potential of some research.
explanation.definitionFit: Exploration is investigation of the unknown, which is what research means in a broad sense.

clue.text: Gradually withdrew from stage act and, ignoring the odds, quit

parts.note: a phase is a stage in a process
to do is to act

indicators.note: ignoring the odd-numbered letters leaves only the even ones

parts.note: the second and fourth letters of quit

explanation.surface: An actor, defying the odds, quit the stage altogether.
explanation.walkthrough: Stage and act suggest the theatre, but stage is a step in a process and act simply means do.
explanation.definitionFit: To phase out something is to remove it in planned steps over time rather than all at once.

clue.text: Risk travelling quiet road before battle

indicators.note: travelling moves things about, so these letters are rearranged
before places the road piece ahead of the quiet piece

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
MI stands for the M1, Britain's main north-south motorway
sh is the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Soldiers take a risk travelling a quiet road before a battle.
explanation.walkthrough: Before is the order signal: the road piece comes before the quiet piece, not after.
explanation.definitionFit: A skirmish is a short, unplanned fight, a small-scale battle.

clue.text: Parking's cut into land for amphibian

definitions.note: loosely; a terrapin is strictly a reptile

indicators.note: cut into means inserted within, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: terrain is ground or land
P is the road-sign symbol for parking

explanation.surface: A car park has been carved into a stretch of habitat used by amphibians.
explanation.definitionFit: A terrapin is a freshwater turtle that lives both in water and on land, so it is loosely called amphibious.

clue.text: Watches castle with boy following return of pipistrelles, perhaps

indicators.note: following places the boy piece after the rest

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle

indicators.note: return means going back, so the word is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: pipistrelles are a kind of small bat
a son is a boy

explanation.surface: A conservationist watches a castle where a boy follows the bats returning to roost.
explanation.definitionFit: To keep tabs on someone is an idiom for monitoring them closely.

clue.text: Fling with fellow in a travelling show

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: in places the fellow piece inside the other words

parts.note: a travelling fair is a funfair that moves from town to town
F is the abbreviation for fellow

explanation.surface: A romance with a man working at a travelling fair.
explanation.definitionFit: An affair is a brief romantic or sexual relationship, which is what a fling is.

clue.text: Complaint with half the Te Deum being played on a pipe

indicators.note: half means only one half of the name is kept and the rest dropped

parts.note: flu is an illness, a complaint
the Te Deum is a Latin hymn of praise

explanation.surface: A sick church musician manages only half the Te Deum on the organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Fluted describes music played on a flute, a kind of pipe.

clue.text: Exceptional religious studies by artist

indicators.note: by means next to, so the two pieces sit side by side

parts.note: RA is a Royal Academician, an artist
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: An artist has made an outstanding contribution to religious studies.
explanation.definitionFit: Something rare is uncommon or unusual, so it stands out from the ordinary.

clue.text: Lovely day with eastern radiance briefly complete

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the word loses its final letter

parts.note: D is the abbreviation for day
E is the abbreviation for east
radiance is light
full means complete

explanation.surface: A lovely day, full of sunshine from the east.
explanation.definitionFit: Delightful means highly pleasing or charming, close in sense to lovely.

clue.text: Problem that is hampering American warship's return

indicators.note: hampering blocks the way from within, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, that is

indicators.note: return means going back the way it came, so the letters are read backwards

parts.note: USS, United States Ship, prefixes US Navy vessel names

explanation.surface: A problem holds up the return of an American warship to port.
explanation.definitionFit: An issue is a matter of concern or difficulty, as in having issues with something.

clue.text: Set up soldier with Juliet to join square dances

indicators.note: join means the square piece is attached on the end

parts.note: Juliet is J in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means turned to read upwards

parts.note: a GI is an American soldier
S is an occasional abbreviation for square

explanation.surface: A soldier and his partner Juliet get ready to join in the square dancing.
explanation.walkthrough: Square dances reads as one phrase, but square is part of the wordplay and dances alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Jigs are lively folk dances, especially associated with Ireland and Scotland.

clue.text: Puts away jug island woman's brought round

parts.note: I is the abbreviation for island

indicators.note: brought round means wrapped around another piece, enclosing it

parts.note: Ms is a woman's title
jug is slang for prison

explanation.surface: An island woman is putting away a jug she has brought round.
explanation.walkthrough: Jug looks like a pitcher being put away, but it is slang for jail.
explanation.definitionFit: To put someone away is an informal idiom for locking them up, which is what imprisons means.

clue.text: When filling cobblers, cook in the oven

indicators.note: filling goes inside something, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: cobblers is British slang for nonsense, as is rot
as can mean when, as in as I left

explanation.surface: A recipe step for fruit cobblers: fill them, then put them in the oven.
explanation.walkthrough: Cobblers suggests the baked fruit pudding, which fits the oven, but it is slang for rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: To roast is to cook food with dry heat, typically meat or vegetables baked in an oven.

clue.text: Implies criminal isn't wearing headgear

indicators.note: wearing puts something on, so one piece is covered by the other
criminal means bent or crooked, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the four letters rearranged
a hat is headgear

explanation.surface: Someone suggests a person isn't a crook just because they wear a hat.
explanation.definitionFit: To hint at something is to suggest it indirectly, which is what implying means.

clue.text: Guaranteed end-user review

indicators.note: review reworks something, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: the seven letters rearranged, ignoring the hyphen

explanation.surface: A guaranteed customer review of a product.
explanation.definitionFit: To ensure something is to make certain that it happens, the same as guaranteeing it.
